title: Newbie question：Burned through my free credits on Tripo, Meshy, Luma, Hitem3D, Rodin. Which one is actually worth a sub?
author: Charming-Touch5379
selftext:
I’m completely new to 3D (trying to make some assets for a personal project but learning Blender is slow). I decided to test out a few of these AI generators just to get some base meshes to start with.
I ran the same concept art through the free trials on Tripo, Meshy, Luma, Hitem3D, Rodin. Honestly? To my untrained eye, they all look... kinda similar?

Since Hitem3D 2.0 is the newest update on the block, does that make it the best current option for the price? Or is Rodin still the king despite the cost? I don't want to waste money on a sub if they are all basically using the same underlying tech. Would love some advice from anyone who uses these in a real workflow.

comments.author: AndresGS_dev
comments.body:
I’m not a professional either, but if you’re just getting started, from my experience I’d recommend Hunyuan. You don’t need a paid plan. It gives you 20 free credits per day, which is great for experimenting without spending money.

Right now there are two versions, a Chinese one and a global one. If you sign up with the same email, you can use both, so you end up with around 40 free credits per day. The global version is usually faster for uploads and downloads, while the Chinese one can be a bit buggy at times, but it has more features, like its built-in 3D studio and workflow system.

The workflow feature feels limited and still in development, which is probably why you can’t really make custom workflows yet and can only use the default ones. That said, the default workflows are actually pretty solid, and they give you a fully finished model with textures and everything. From what I’ve seen, they don’t consume credits, so they’re nice for learning and generating base assets.

I’d still recommend learning at least some basic Blender, since you’ll almost always need to clean up meshes, fix topology, or tweak textures no matter which AI tool you use. And if I got anything wrong here, feel free to correct me.

If you’re considering a paid plan, this site is also useful for comparing max-quality outputs from different paid 3D AI tools: [https://www.top3d.ai](https://www.top3d.ai)
